text.p: Salomon Brothers raised its 1996 and 1997 earnings estimate for Agan Chemical Manufacturers Ltd and maintained its buy recommendation after the Israeli company reported better-than-expected third-quarter results.
"We remain bullish on Agan and view the company as becoming a true global operator in the agrochemicals business," analyst Victor Halpert said in a report.
Salomon raised its 1996 net income projection to $25.6 million or $1.70 a share versus from $24.2 million or $1.61. In 1995 the company earned $1.36 a share.
Its 1997 estimate was raised to $27.5 million or $1.83 from $26.8 million or $1.78 a share previously.
In the third quarter Agan earned $0.27 a share, up 46 percent from a year earlier and above Salomon's projection of $0.21.
"Our 12-month price target is $25 per share or 80 shekels," Halpert said. The shares are trading at 55.91 shekels.

Halpert said the shares were attractively valued at 9.3 times forecast 1997 earnings per share and 8.2 times 1998 estimates, "well below its international peers and the local market Mishtanim Index average".
Agan and its parent Makhteshim Chemical Works will merge their agrochemical operations into a new holding company next May.
"This new entity should result in an improved long-term valuation and boost the company's ability to raise financing on the capital markets," Halpert said.
